transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to meet. As you know, next Thursday we'll be conducting a student-family reunification exercise following a simulated building evacuation. Before I can sign off on the final operating plan and we send the notice to families, I need to check in with each of you. The current draft has the gymnasium as our reunification site, a single transportation wave, an on-site medication table, and English-only pickup forms. I'd like to hear from each of you — the nurse, facilities coordinator, transportation coordinator, and family liaison — on whether you see any issues or have recommendations before I approve. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a transportation issue with the draft plan. I confirmed this week that the exercise group includes 96 students, and we have only one available 50-seat bus because the second bus is assigned to another school. Transportation policy therefore requires exactly two bus waves — not one. The draft currently assumes a single wave, which would leave 46 students without transport. This needs to be corrected before the plan is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a language-access issue with the draft plan. My family contact review, which I completed this week, shows that Spanish and Somali are the two additional languages needed for pickup instructions among our families. The plan must provide pickup forms in English, Spanish, and Somali, and we need to have an interpreter available. Right now, the draft only includes English-only pickup forms, and the language-access details haven't been entered yet. This needs to be corrected before the plan is finalized and sent to families.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: I need to flag a medication storage issue with the draft plan. My current health-plan list identifies four students whose emergency medications must remain in temperature-controlled storage, and the nurse's office refrigerator is the only approved storage location during the exercise. I confirmed this requirement while reviewing the health plans this week. However, the draft plan still lists an on-site medication table, which would not meet the temperature-controlled storage requirement for these students' medications. This needs to be corrected before the plan is finalized.

To summarize what we've identified: the gymnasium is unavailable and must be changed to the cafeteria, transportation needs two bus waves instead of one, pickup forms must be provided in English, Spanish, and Somali with interpreter support, and the medication arrangement needs to meet temperature-controlled storage requirements rather than using an on-site table. Dr. Vega, it looks like the draft plan needs revisions in all four areas before it can be approved and sent to families. I'd recommend we update the plan to reflect these corrections and circulate a revised draft for final review.
